input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The new minimum wait defaults to one second instead of zero.
- failure path: With default options, an early exponential result below one second is raised to a one-second delay, slowing retries that previously had no configured floor.

Reviewer finding
- description: The new `min` parameter defaults to 1 second, so existing callers that relied on the implicit floor of 0 now get a 1-second minimum wait.
- rationale: Trigger: a caller uses wait_exponential_jitter(initial=0.1) or any call that previously produced a sub-second wait, without passing min. Mechanism: the return value is now max(max(0, 1), min(result, max)), which floors every wait at 1 second. Impact: retry timing changes silently for existing users, with longer sleeps than before and possibly slower tests or retry loops. The title announces a new min parameter, not a changed default, so the default should preserve the old behavior (0).
critique: The finding identifies the same defect: the new min parameter defaults to 1 instead of 0. Through the max/clamp operation, this raises sub-second exponential waits to a one-second floor and slows retries that had no floor before.
